themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Crown Heights is experiencing a convergence of street-level infrastructure failures THIS WEEK: dangling street signs (6 complaints vs. 0.2 weekly average, +2300%), damaged trees (7 complaints vs. 0.8 average, +833%), and deteriorating street conditions (28 complaints vs. 6.0 average, +367%), suggesting potential storm damage or systematic neglect requiring immediate DOT and Parks inspection.
evidence: Street Sign - Dangling: 6 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 13.28)
Damaged Tree: 7 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 9.45)
Street Condition: 28 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.0 weekly average (z-score: 8.98)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent weather events (wind, rain) caused coordinated damage across the district
Request incident reports from DOT and Parks; examine maintenance schedules and budget cuts

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from streets and sidewalks surged to 50 complaints LAST WEEK, a 420% spike over the 8-week average of 9.6 weekly complaints (z-score: 11.31), indicating either construction activity, street vending/commerce, or event-driven disturbances that warrants investigation into source and frequency.
evidence: Noise - Street/Sidewalk: 50 complaints last week vs. 9.6 weekly average (z-score: 11.31, +420%)
No corresponding spike in Noise - Helicopter or Noise - Residential, suggesting localized street-level source
Pattern does not match long-running residential noise baseline
reporting_angles: Canvass blocks with highest concentration of complaints; identify construction sites, street fairs, or vendor clusters
Interview residents about timing and type of noise (machinery, music, crowds)

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Sanitation conditions worsened LAST WEEK with dirty condition complaints at 86 (up 365% vs. 18.5 weekly average) and street sweeping complaints at 6 (up 860% vs. 0.6 average), signaling potential Sanitation Department service gaps or recent contamination event that aligns with Community Board's repeated budget requests for enhanced cleaning.
evidence: Dirty Condition: 86 complaints last week vs. 18.5 weekly average (z-score: 6.44, +365%)
Street Sweeping Complaint: 6 complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 5.42, +860%)
Community Board has repeated 'Other cleaning requests' as standing budget priority, indicating chronic baseline issue
reporting_angles: Request Sanitation Department route schedules and actual collection data for Crown Heights to identify gaps
Visit neighborhood to photograph conditions; interview residents about timing of deterioration

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints jumped to 4 LAST WEEK versus a 0.2 weekly baseline (1500% increase, z-score: 8.66), clustering with broader tree/street infrastructure failures THIS WEEK, suggesting either deliberate vandalism or negligent development activity that warrants Parks enforcement review.
evidence: Illegal Tree Damage: 4 complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 8.66, +1500%)
Converges with Damaged Tree spike (7 THIS WEEK, +833%) suggesting related environmental stress
431 DOB alteration permits filed in last 90 days provide potential construction-related context
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 illegal tree damage complaints with DOB permits to identify if construction activity is damaging trees
Interview Parks enforcement about complaint follow-up and violation patterns

themes_detail.label: General 311 Complaint Surge
themes_detail.summary: A broad uptick in general/unclassified complaints (46 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 17.9 weekly average, +157%) may indicate either reporting system changes, resident frustration leading to non-specific filings, or service failures spanning multiple categories that residents cannot categorize clearly.
evidence: GENERAL complaints: 46 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 17.9 weekly average (z-score: 7.55, +157%)
Timing slightly older than street/sanitation spikes but still within 2-week window
Lacks granular categorization, making root cause diagnosis difficult
reporting_angles: Request sample of general complaints from 311 system to identify common themes residents could not categorize
Assess whether 311 app/website usability issues contributed to misclassification
